title: Home page round 2 — TV remote, Lights tab, Media tab

steps.headline: With the remote closed, which TV card do you like best?
steps.notice: Both themes (Golden Sunbreak and Crème) are shown. Netflix is playing, so the app buttons show Prime Video where Netflix would be. The remote is now a small icon beside the power button.
steps.risk: Closed, all three look almost the same except the app buttons: option C hides them until the remote opens.

variants.label: Machined dial
variants.summary: A dial that looks like brushed metal, with engraved arrows and a domed OK button.
variants.risk: Heaviest and most solid-looking; the metal can feel out of place beside the soft glass cards.

variants.label: Glass jog wheel
variants.summary: A frosted glass wheel in four quarters.
variants.risk: The lit quarter hides behind your thumb on a phone; the sweep is a little showy the first few times.

variants.label: Floating ring
variants.summary: Just a thin outline ring with small arrows, no filled disc.
variants.risk: Lightest and calmest, but with no fill the arrows are less obviously buttons; closed, the card has no app buttons at all.

steps.path: Home > Media > the TV card > remote icon
steps.headline: With the remote open, which dial looks the most premium?
steps.notice: The dial sits above the volume bar, inside the Now playing panel. Back and Home flank the skip and play buttons.
steps.risk: The panel is taller when open, so cards below it move down.

steps.headline: Press the remote icon, then an app button. Which reveal and app swap feels best?
steps.notice: Open and close the remote a few times, press the arrows and OK, then press HBO Max or Disney+: the app on the TV leaves the row and Prime Video slides into its place.
steps.risk: All three add short movement (about a third of a second) and all stop if the computer is set to reduce motion. The pretend TV answers app presses after a short delay, like a real one.

variants.label: Machined dial
variants.summary: The dial grows out of the remote icon with a small spring. The app that leaves shrinks away and Prime drops in from above.
variants.risk: The dial travels the furthest, so it is the most movement on screen.

variants.label: Glass jog wheel
variants.summary: The panel stretches down while the volume row slides lower and the wheel fades in with a sweep of light. The old app slides out left, Prime slides in from the right.
variants.risk: The panel's stretch moves everything beneath it for a moment.

variants.label: Floating ring
variants.summary: The ring unfolds down from the header like a flap, then the app buttons fade up. The old app lifts away and Prime rises into place. Presses ripple.
variants.risk: The flap is a 3-D turn, which some people find flashy on a small card.

steps.headline: Which card layout makes switching, dimming and changing a room's lights simplest on the Lights tab?
steps.notice: Each room is now ONE card named like "Destin's Room Lights", with All off, the scenes button and a fold arrow in its header. Destin's Room is open; the unreachable TV backlight sits last.
steps.risk: All three keep what you decided: cards and colour menus start closed, scenes behind the palette button, the slider handle stays attached.

variants.label: Today
variants.summary: The Lights tab as it is now: a room card with a Lights card nested inside it.
variants.risk: Two cards for one room; the room name and "Lights" are separate headings.

variants.label: Room strip
variants.summary: One card per room, called "Destin's Room Lights". A big brightness bar for the whole room sits on top, with an All off button; open the card and each light is a slim row with its own thin bar and colour dot.
variants.risk: Slim rows are small to hit on a phone, and every light still needs its bar dragged precisely.

variants.label: Tile grid
variants.summary: One card per room. Under the room bar each light is a square tile: tap to switch it, drag it sideways to dim it, and its fill shows how bright it is. The coloured dot opens its colours.
variants.risk: Tap and drag share one surface, so a slow, wobbly tap can dim a light instead of switching it; drag is not discoverable until tried.

variants.label: Mixer
variants.summary: One card per room. Each light is a tall fader standing side by side like a sound desk, with the whole-room fader first. The bulb on top switches a light; the dot underneath opens its colours.
variants.risk: Looks the most different from the rest of the page; with many lights it wraps to a second row.

steps.notice: The same open room on a 390 px wide screen.
steps.risk: The mixer wraps onto a second row; the title can take two lines.

steps.headline: Where do unreachable lights and rooms end up?

steps.risk: A room that comes back on moves back up on the next refresh.

steps.headline: Switch the whole room off, dim it, then change one light. Which feels the most obvious?
steps.notice: In Destin's Room press All off, then All on. Drag the room bar. Switch one light and dim it (tiles: tap, or drag sideways; mixer: pull a fader). Press the paint palette for scenes and a colour dot for colours. Press the arrow to fold the card.
steps.risk: Everything here is practice data; nothing reaches a real light.

steps.headline: Which layout should the Media tab use, so what is playing is easy to see and control?
steps.notice: Room boxes are gone: every speaker and TV is its own card, named like 'Destin's Room TV'. Playing first, then paused, idle, off, and speakers that are not responding last, dimmed.
steps.risk: All three re-sort when something starts or stops: a card you just paused moves down the page.

variants.label: Now playing hero
variants.summary: Big cards across the top for what is playing, with album-style colour, the title, large play, skip and volume. Paused ones sit under their own heading. Quiet devices become slim rows with one button: Play or Turn on.
variants.risk: The playing cards are tall, so a house with four things playing needs scrolling before you reach the idle devices.

variants.label: Stage and shelf
variants.summary: Playing and paused devices are wide cards with the controls on one line. Everything else sits on a shelf of small square tiles, each with one round button (play or power).
variants.risk: Tiles are small, so names and states wrap onto two lines; a long speaker name gets cut.

variants.label: One list, live rows
variants.summary: One simple column. A coloured bar on the left says the state: yellow playing, amber paused, grey idle, red not responding. Playing rows open up to show controls; the rest stay a single line.
variants.risk: The least dramatic: nothing is much bigger than anything else, so it is quieter to look at but less eye-catching.

steps.headline: When speakers play together, which layout makes them read as one thing?
steps.notice: Here Destin's Room and Roam 2 play one song. Each shows as ONE card or row, not two.
steps.risk: Grouped speakers share one title and one set of skip buttons; only volume can differ per speaker.

variants.label: Hero with a Together box
variants.summary: One big card. A 'Playing together' box inside lists each speaker with its own volume bar.
variants.risk: The tallest of the three, since every speaker gets its own bar.

variants.label: Wide card with name chips
variants.summary: One wide card with a linked 'Playing together' strip of speaker chips, and one volume bar.
variants.risk: You cannot set one speaker louder than the other from the card; that needs the Group bar.

variants.label: Row with a linked line
variants.summary: One row whose second line reads 'Destin's Room + Roam 2 together' with a link mark.
variants.risk: The smallest hint that two speakers are involved; easy to miss.

steps.headline: Press play, pause, skip and volume in each. Which one feels easiest?
steps.notice: These are the working page with a pretend house. The TV's remote is only a small round icon for now; its own design is decided separately.
steps.risk: Pressing pause or play moves the card to a new place in the list, which may feel like a jump.

variants.label: Now playing hero
variants.summary: Big cards for what is playing; slim rows for the rest.

variants.label: Stage and shelf
variants.summary: Wide cards on top, small square tiles below.

variants.label: One list, live rows
variants.summary: One column; playing rows open up, the rest stay one line.
